text:
marta: quick heads-up — noticed after last night's deploy that sticky routing by header (`x-rw-version`) is still taking precedence for some long-lived clients. console shows traffic as v2 but backend routes them to v1 variants, so dashboards and quota math are wrong :grimacing:

alex: ugh. do we have a repro sample or tenant id?

marta: repro curl below (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\ 
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer XXXX\" \\ 
  -H \"x-rw-version: v1\" \\ 
  -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
If client includes `x-rw-version: v1` but route default is v2, runtime is honoring sticky cookie/header and falling back to v1 pool.

jun: are sticky signals intended to survive across model rollouts? i thought we only sticky on session cookie, not on header. header should be highest precedence (explicit override) or lowest (legacy). which design did we agree on? :thinking:

marta: older decision doc said header was a soft-hint for compatibility with SDKs, but we didn't formalize precedence vs console pin. looks like implementation treated header like a persistent affinity key.

alex: quick mitigation: we can change precedence so explicit `?version=` query param > console pin > ephemeral header > cookie. that would make console toggles more authoritative for rollouts. low-risk patch?

sam: main worry = billing/quotas. if console says v2 (bill at v2 rates) but tokens executed on v1, customers get billed wrong. need immediate telemetry to detect mismatch and a safe rollback path.

marta: agreed. proposing 2 immediate steps: 1) emit `compat.sticky_mismatch=1` whenever request header version != routed model version; 2) add a console flag to globally ignore sticky header for a tenant (soft kill switch).

jun: +1 on metric. add tags: `tenant_id`, `route`, `console_view_version`, `routed_model_version`. dashboard tile should show mismatch rate by tenant, percent of tokens mismatched, and last change.

ops-bot: deploy started: runtime-v2.3.1 -> canary pool (10%) at 23:12 UTC.

alex: for the ignore-sticky toggle, UX question: should it be immediate (hard switch) or queued with canary? if immediate, support teams can flip it quickly for a tenant. i prefer immediate but audit-logged.

sam: immediate is fine if we restrict to account admins and add an audit log entry and optional grace period where console shows a preview of expected routing changes. ops needs an escape hatch.

marta: implementation notes: code change is small in router precedence table. we'll also add the metric emission in the middleware path so it's visible before we flip precedence. PR will include unit test and e2e with a fake sticky header.

jun: also add a small warning banner in console rollout page: \"Detected clients with sticky compatibility headers. Flipping version precedence may change routing for some sessions.\" include link to runbook. :warning:

sam: create a billing alert that triggers if mismatch tokens > 1% of traffic for a tenant for 10 minutes. also surface candidate tenants in the console so PMs can proactively reach out.

marta: action items:
- alex: patch router precedence + tests (PR today)
- jun: dashboard panels + alert (this PM)
- sam: billing alert + audit log requirements (today)
- i'll add console toggle and danger banner (tomorrow)

alex: starting PR now. will tag everyone for review.

ops-bot: deploy success: runtime-v2.3.1 canary -> 10% (23:20 UTC).

marta: thanks — keeping an eye on `compat.sticky_mismatch`. will ping when we see signal. :eyes:
